inputCoverage.osmSnapshot: 2026-08-11 Protomaps z14; 6×6 tile window before our conflation
inputCoverage.agencyScope: Complete features intersecting input window from existing source cache; not a fresh agency census

recommendation.summary: Review a segment-level merge: keep one overlapping alignment and verify the outlying sections as possible unique ends or branches. Do not connect them automatically.
reasons: OpenStreetMap: 73% of its geometry lies within 15 m of the other source; 76% within 50 m. Median nearest-line offset 4.5 m.
NPS: 97% of its geometry lies within 15 m of the other source; 100% within 50 m. Median nearest-line offset 3.9 m.

Within the same input window, OpenStreetMap: 2,772 m long, median vertex spacing 24.8 m, 652 m outside the other source’s 50 m corridor; NPS: 2,067 m long, median vertex spacing 9.5 m, 0 m outside the other source’s 50 m corridor.

Endpoint check: OpenStreetMap has 3 non-seam endpoint candidates over 75 m from the other alignment; NPS has 0 non-seam endpoint candidates over 75 m from the other alignment. These can be real additions, branches, or source gaps; inspect their connections.

DEM sanity check in the shared corridor: OpenStreetMap: 90th-percentile absolute terrain grade 17.4% over 23 sampled 50 m sections; NPS: 90th-percentile absolute terrain grade 17.0% over 29 sampled 50 m sections. Lower grade alone does not mean a route is more accurate.
Vertex density measures representation detail, not survey accuracy. Sharp turns may be genuine switchbacks; geometry alone cannot diagnose GPS multipath.
recommendation.limitations: Heuristic guidance, not an independent ground-truth verdict. Uses source geometry and frozen DEM only; no imagery interpretation or route editing. DEM measures ground surface, not surveyed trail elevation. Full agency inputs and OSM tile fragments have different lineage; no automatic edits.
